chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about tayammum. So he struck the ground with his two palms, then wiped his face with them. Then he struck the ground with his left hand and wiped with it from his elbow to the fingertips, once over its outer side and once over its inner side. Then he struck the ground with his right hand, then did with his left as he had done with his right. Then he said: “This is tayammum for that in which ghusl is required. And in wudu (ablution), the face and the two hands up to the elbows [are included], and what there had been wiping over is omitted: the head and the two feet are not subjected to tayammum with earth.”

As for what this hadith contains, that he wiped from the elbow to the fingertips, once over its outer side and once over its inner side, its meaning is what has previously been mentioned in the interpretation of the report of Samāʿah which ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from him: that what is intended by it is the ruling, not the act itself. It is as though he said: he wiped over the back of his palm, and thereby attained the ruling of one who washed his hand from the elbow, its outer and inner sides. This does not invalidate what we have held.

If someone says: The first two reports—one of them from Abū Baṣīr Layth al-Murādī from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and the second from Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām al-Kindī from al-Riḍā عليه السلام—together with the report narrated by Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā from al-ʿAlāʾ from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from one of them both عليهما السلام, do not outwardly indicate that the two strikes or the two times are specifically for ghusl of janābah rather than for wudu (ablution). So from where do you say that it is restricted to the ruling of janābah? Why did you not say, as others have held, that the obligation in wudu (ablution) also is two times?

It is said to him: When many reports are established indicating that the obligation in tayammum is once, once, then these reports came containing two strikes, we interpret what contains the ruling of once as referring to wudu (ablution), and what contains the ruling of twice as referring to ghusl of janābah, so that the reports do not contradict one another. Moreover, we have already cited two reports that explain these reports: one of them from Ḥarīz from Zurārah from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and the other from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, stating that tayammum in place of wudu (ablution) is once, and in place of janābah is twice. And among the reports that came indicating the obligation of once in an unrestricted manner is the previously mentioned report of Ibn Bukayr from Zurārah, and also.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, dry ablution performed with earth or clean ground substitute
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: earth or clean ground material used for tayammum
key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the report
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl, ritual bath required in states such as janabah
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ: the two elbows, the legal limit mentioned for the hands

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the difference between one-strike and two-strike tayammum?
ai.summary: This report discusses the method and legal understanding of tayammum, including how it is performed and how differing narrations are reconciled. It explains that one strike is understood for tayammum replacing wudu (ablution), while two strikes are understood for tayammum replacing ghusl due to janabah, in order to harmonize the reports.
